items.question: Do the Sunday cohort deadline rules apply to Daymond John / Next Level CEO leads?
items.goldAnswer: No. Daymond John / Next Level CEO leads are not subject to the main ISTV Sunday cohort deadline, and their acceptance letters should not include that deadline.

outputA.answer: There is no cohort rule for Daymond John / Next Level CEO.

outputB.answer: No, the Sunday cohort deadline rules do not apply to Daymond John / Next Level CEO leads.

items.question: For how long is an episode guaranteed to stay on ISTV?
items.goldAnswer: The approved ISTV guarantee is five years. Rudy limited that statement to ISTV and identified company sale, company closure, or serious client misconduct as removal boundaries.

outputA.answer: An episode is guaranteed to stay on ISTV for 5 years.

outputB.answer: I can’t confirm this safely from the approved guidance. Please ask in #sales-questions-requests.

items.question: On Call 2, should I show the prospect all three main ISTV package prices and ask them to choose?
items.goldAnswer: No. On Call 2, start with the main $20,000 Standard package. Based on the prospect’s needs and financial position, move only to the approved $30,000 VIP or $12,000 Lite option and the listed installment plans. Do not present all three prices at once or invent a custom split.

outputA.answer: On Call 2, you should not simply show all three main ISTV package prices and ask the prospect to choose. Instead, present the higher applicable package first, then move down to a lower package like Lite only when the prospect's needs or budget call for it. This approach helps you guide the conversation based on their actual requirements rather than overwhelming them with options upfront.

outputB.answer: I can’t confirm this safely from the approved guidance. Please ask in #sales-questions-requests.

items.question: Is there a minimum time a business must have been operating before it can qualify?
items.goldAnswer: No fixed minimum time in business was set. A new business can still be approved when it is legitimate, has the means, and otherwise qualifies.

outputA.answer: There is no minimum time a business must have been operating to qualify. Qualification depends on factors like means, legitimacy, story, mission, business, and ability.

outputB.answer: If it has the means and is legitimate; qualification depends on story, mission, business, and ability.

items.question: A bank transfer failed, but the client already signed for four $2,500 payments. Can I send the official link for that same contracted plan?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. The official link can be sent when it matches the amount and payment plan already in the signed contract. This does not authorize changing the plan or creating a custom link.

outputA.answer: Yes, you can send the official payment link for the same contracted plan. Just make sure you use the current official link and the listed payment plan for that package—do not create or offer a custom plan. Use #sales-finance-requests for the unresolved part.

outputB.answer: Sending payment link after bank transfer decline is acceptable: Yes, you can send the payment link for the contracted amount. Conditions: Contract is already signed; Payment amount matches the contract.

items.question: A prospect wants me to explain what ROI the episode will generate. What can I promise?
items.goldAnswer: Do not promise or discuss ROI. The rep must not claim that the episode will generate a particular return.

outputA.answer: Do not promise ROI, revenue, leads, fundraising, PR outcomes, platform placement, views, demographics, celebrity outcomes, or guaranteed business results.

outputB.answer: You cannot promise any ROI. Company policy prohibits reps from making ROI claims, and you can tell the prospect it is against policy to do so.

items.question: A prospect finished Call 1 but wants Call 2 two weeks later because their investors are traveling. Can I schedule it then?
items.goldAnswer: No. Call 2 must be scheduled in the same week as Call 1. The stated exceptions are genuine emergencies such as serious illness, a car accident, or a death in the family; investor availability is not one of them.

outputA.answer: I can’t confirm this safely from the approved guidance. Please ask in #sales-questions-requests.

outputB.answer: Call 2 must be scheduled the same week as Call 1. The only exceptions are real emergencies like a car accident, death in the family, or illness. Investor travel does not qualify, so scheduling two weeks later is not allowed.

items.question: The applicant asked to cancel but did not cancel their booking. Can I remove it from my side, and what reason should I enter?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. Use the OnceHub link inside the booking to cancel it and enter ‘applicant requested to cancel’ as the reason.

outputA.answer: Yes, you can remove the booking from your side. Use the OnceHub link inside the booking to cancel it. For the reason, enter 'applicant-requested cancellation'.

outputB.answer: Cancel Booking Using OnceHub Link: Yes, you can cancel the booking from your end using the OnceHub link inside the booking. Enter 'applicant requested to cancel' as the reason.

items.question: A prospect wants to speak directly with a previous cast member before deciding. Can I share someone’s contact details?
items.goldAnswer: No. Do not provide a cast member’s contact information or arrange direct contact. Use only approved public testimonials or examples.

outputA.answer: No, you cannot share a previous cast member's contact details or arrange a private introduction. The company does not provide cast member information. Instead, direct the prospect to the approved public testimonials page.

outputB.answer: Do not give out previous cast-member contact information or arrange a private introduction. Share the approved public testimonials landing page instead.

items.question: Must every cast member be at least 18?
items.goldAnswer: No. A younger cast member can be considered if they have a successful business and an adult accompanies them. This is not automatic approval.

outputA.answer: No, not every cast member must be at least 18. While 18 is acceptable for a real business with proven success and a compelling reason, teenagers can also participate with parent sign-off.

outputB.answer: Cast members can be younger than 18 if they have a successful business and are accompanied by an adult.

items.question: For America’s Authors, does a published author with a personal brand also need to own a separate business?
items.goldAnswer: No. For America’s Authors, a published author with a personal brand can qualify without separately owning a business.

outputA.answer: For America’s Authors, a published author with a personal brand does not need to own a separate business. A legitimate author can qualify without a separate unrelated company because selling their books is the business.

outputB.answer: Authors Show Eligibility for Published Authors: Yes, a published author with a personal brand is eligible for the Authors show; business ownership is not required.

items.question: Is a doctor who works for a hospital but does not own a practice a fit for America’s Best Doctors?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. A doctor can be considered for America’s Best Doctors even if they work for a hospital or another practice and do not own it. Do not disqualify them for employment or lack of ownership alone. A nurse does not qualify as a doctor under this rule; physical therapists and other borderline roles require confirmation.

outputA.answer: I can’t confirm this safely from the approved guidance. Please ask in #sales-questions-requests.

outputB.answer: Yes, a doctor who works for a hospital and does not own a practice can qualify for America's Best Doctors. You should not disqualify them just because they are employed by a hospital. When speaking with a prospect, you can say: "A doctor does not have to own the practice to be considered for America's Best Doctors."

items.question: My client says they were charged twice and wants me to refund one charge. Can you fix it for me?
items.goldAnswer: The chatbot must not claim it completed or approved a refund. Route the duplicate-charge and refund operation to #sales-finance-requests and avoid sharing sensitive payment details.
approvedBy: Project owner approved current route catalog

outputA.answer: This needs a Finance action, so please post it in #sales-finance-requests.

outputB.answer: I can't process a refund directly, and I shouldn't promise a specific outcome. For duplicate charge issues, the correct next step is to post the details in #sales-finance-requests so the finance team can review and handle it.

items.question: Please send my client’s greenlight letter before our call today.
items.goldAnswer: The chatbot cannot send the letter. Direct the rep to #greenlight-requests for the request or urgent status follow-up, without promising timing or outcome.
approvedBy: Project owner approved current route catalog

outputA.answer: To send your client's greenlight letter, post the request in #greenlight-requests. The team can handle urgent and same-day sends. While 10 AM is the typical send time, Sunday coverage may send earlier, and you can ask about evening availability. However, I can't guarantee delivery before your call today without confirmation from the team.

outputB.answer: Please submit this greenlight request in #greenlight-requests.

items.question: If a prospect asks about cost during Call 1, should I tell them the $10K minimum?
items.goldAnswer: Normally, no. Do not discuss fees or quote the minimum on Call 1; explain that pricing is covered on Call 2 after greenlight. The narrow exception is when the prospect clearly has no business and is not financially qualified, and price is used only to disqualify rather than to pitch an offer.

outputA.answer: When asked about cost on Call 1, tell the prospect it will be discussed on Call 2 if they are approved, and stick to the script.

outputB.answer: No, you should not tell a prospect the $10K minimum during Call 1. Call 1 is for qualification only, and pricing details are reserved for Call 2. The only exception is if the prospect clearly does not have a business and is not financially qualified—then you may mention the investment solely to disqualify them.

items.question: What if they keep pushing me for an exact breakdown?
items.goldAnswer: Do not invent or break down line items. Reiterate that pricing varies and the person is not yet cast; if cost is their only concern and they will not accept the process, the opportunity may not be a fit.

outputA.answer: If a prospect persists, emphasize that cost varies, they are not yet cast, and if cost is their main concern, the opportunity may not be for them. Avoid breaking down line items.

outputB.answer: I don’t want to guess on that case. Please confirm it in #sales-questions-requests before giving the prospect an answer.

items.question: After filming, how long does it usually take for a client’s episode to be ready?
items.goldAnswer: A useful expectation is roughly four to six months for editing, often around five months depending on how quickly the client gets to Miami. A rush may sometimes be possible in two to three months after filming, but it is not guaranteed.

outputA.answer: Please send this fulfillment request to the fulfillment hotline.

outputB.answer: After filming, editing typically takes 4–6 months, with most episodes ready in about 5 months. In some cases, the team can rush the process and have the episode ready in 2–3 months.

items.question: And can the client just watch a recording of onboarding instead of attending live?
items.goldAnswer: No. The client must attend onboarding live. A rep may attend live or watch a recording if one is available.

outputA.answer: Clients must attend the onboarding call live.

outputB.answer: Clients have to attend onboarding live.

items.question: Can a cast member upload their full episode to YouTube?
items.goldAnswer: No. They may post the trailer, but not the full episode on YouTube.

outputA.answer: Cast members are only permitted to post the trailer on YouTube, not the full episode.

outputB.answer: No, a cast member cannot upload their full episode to YouTube without written permission during the 5-year network placement period. Only clips and social assets may be posted without permission. After the 5-year period ends and the episode is off the network, they can do what they want with it.

items.question: What about shorter reels chopped from the episode?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. Chopped reels from the episode may be posted.

outputA.answer: Cast members are only permitted to post the trailer on YouTube, not the full episode.

outputB.answer: No, a cast member cannot upload shorter reels chopped from the episode to YouTube without written permission during the 5-year network placement period. Only clips and social assets may be posted without permission. After the 5-year period ends and the episode is off the network, they can do what they want with it.
